title: Strict mode strikes
brief:
Run this before you change anything. It fails instantly - no 30-second wait - and the message tells you why.

The home page has **two** links called *Test Cases*: one in the menu, one as a big button in the banner. That is not a bug in the shop; the real automationexercise.com does the same, which is why `learn/test_tc07_test_cases_page.py` has a comment about it.

Make the test pass. The menu link and the banner button go to the same place, so either will do - just say which one you mean.
starter:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_test_cases_page_opens(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/")

    page.get_by_role("link", name="Test Cases").click()

    expect(page).to_have_url("https://automationexercise.com/test_cases")
    expect(page.get_by_text("Below is the list of test Cases")).to_be_visible()
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_test_cases_page_opens(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/")

    # .first because the page has more than one 'Test Cases' link
    # (one in the menu, one big button in the banner).
    page.get_by_role("link", name="Test Cases").first.click()

    expect(page).to_have_url("https://automationexercise.com/test_cases")
    expect(page.get_by_text("Below is the list of test Cases")).to_be_visible()

checks.label: The click lands on the test cases page
checks.feedback: The shop never got there. If you are still seeing a strict mode violation, the locator is still matching both links.

checks.name: to_be_visible
checks.label: The page content assertion still runs

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: The error says "resolved to 2 elements". You do not need a different locator - you need to say which of the two.

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: Three ways: .first, .nth(0), or scope the search to the menu with page.locator(".shop-menu").get_by_role(...). All three are legitimate here.

reveal:
Strict mode looks like an obstacle and is actually a gift. The alternative - most other tools' behaviour - is silently clicking the first match, which means your test passes today and clicks the wrong thing next month when the order changes.

A failure you can read beats a pass you cannot trust.
